paragraphs: We are a late clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing transformative treatments for patients with serious immunological diseases. Our lead product candidate, atacicept, is currently being evaluated for the treatment of immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) and other autoimmune kidney diseases. Atacicept is a native human TACI-Fc fusion protein that binds both the B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) cytokines and is self-administered subcutaneously at home. We are conducting ORIGIN 3, the pivotal Phase 3 trial of atacicept 150 mg in IgAN. The trial met the primary efficacy endpoint of reduction in proteinuria as measured by 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) at week 36, where participants treated with atacicept achieved a 46% reduction from baseline in UPCR with a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 42% reduction in UPCR compared to placebo (p<0.0001). The incidence of adverse events was generally balanced between the atacicept and placebo groups, with fewer serious adverse events reported with atacicept (n=1 [0.5%]) than placebo (n=11 [5%]), no safety signals indicating immunosuppression, and no deaths in either treatment group. In November 2025, we submitted a Biologics License Application (BLA) for atacicept for the treatment of adults with IgAN to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) through the Accelerated Approval Program. On January 7, 2026, the FDA granted priority review to the application and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of July 7, 2026. If approved, atacicept would be the first B-cell modulator inhibiting both BAFF and APRIL for IgAN, offering patients an autoinjector for at-home self-administration. The ORIGIN 3 key secondary endpoint to support full approval is estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at 104 weeks, with results expected in 2027.

The ORIGIN Phase 2b clinical trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of atacicept in 116 participants with IgAN and reported positive results at 24 weeks in January 2023, 36 weeks in June 2023, and 96 weeks in October 2024. The trial remained blinded through 36 weeks, after which all participants were eligible for the open label extension portion of the study and received atacicept 150 mg through 96 weeks. Atacicept met its primary endpoint at 24 weeks with a statistically significant reduction in UPCR. Through 36 weeks, participants treated with atacicept demonstrated reductions in galactose-deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1, the autoantigen produced by B cells in patients with IgAN), hematuria, and UPCR, with stable eGFR. The improvements in Gd-IgA1, hematuria, UPCR and eGFR represent the quartet of findings consistent with IgAN disease modification. The 96-week open label extension results showed consistent and sustained reductions in Gd-IgA1, hematuria, and UPCR, with continued eGFR stabilization at a rate similar to the general population without kidney disease. Atacicept's safety profile appeared favorable, and comparable to placebo, across the ORIGIN program in IgAN.

We believe that atacicept has pipeline-in-a-molecule potential, with expected application in multiple diseases. Based on data from the ORIGIN Phase 2b trial, the FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation to atacicept for the treatment of IgAN. We have also committed to providing long-term access to atacicept for ORIGIN participants through ORIGIN EXTEND, a long-term Phase 2 extension study that offers atacicept to participants who completed ORIGIN Phase 2b or 3 until, if approved, commercial availability in their country or region. We are evaluating atacicept in other autoimmune kidney diseases, including primary membranous nephropathy (pMN), focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) and minimal change disease (MCD), in patients with anti-phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) or anti-nephrin autoantibodies in the Phase 2 PIONEER clinical trial. Potential future indications include anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV), lupus nephritis (LN), Sjogren's disease, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), systemic sclerosis, generalized myasthenia gravis, and idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura.

We also hold worldwide, exclusive development and commercial rights to MAU868, a potentially first-in-class monoclonal antibody to treat reactivated BK virus (BKV) infections, for which we completed a Phase 2 clinical trial in 2022. In January 2025, we acquired worldwide, exclusive development and commercial rights to VT-109, a novel, next-generation dual BAFF/APRIL inhibitor that is in preclinical development. We believe that our current pipeline programs leverage the deep expertise of our team and have strong potential commercial synergies.

Beyond our lead indication in IgAN, we have several late-stage opportunities for potential patient benefit – including indication expansion opportunities for atacicept, the development of VT-109 in B-cell–mediated diseases, and MAU868 for BK viremia among kidney transplant recipients. We are currently evaluating these opportunities for future development.

As part of our life cycle management strategy for atacicept, we are actively enrolling participants in a monthly dose range finding study to evaluate extended dosing intervals. As discussed above, there are also multiple indications in which blocking BAFF and APRIL may offer therapeutic benefit and which offer an attractive commercial opportunity, some of which we are evaluating in the PIONEER phase 2 clinical trial.

In January 2025, we announced a license agreement (Stanford Agreement) with the Board of Trustees of Leland Stanford Junior University (Stanford) to acquire global rights to VT-109, a novel, next generation fusion protein targeting BAFF and APRIL that is in preclinical development with wide therapeutic potential across the spectrum of B-cell-mediated diseases. These rights are for all therapeutic, prophylactic, diagnostic, and treatment uses in humans.

Finally, we have exclusive worldwide rights, pursuant to the license agreement (Novartis License) with Novartis International Pharmaceutical AG (Novartis), to the investigational drug MAU868 for BK viremia among kidney transplant recipients. BKV is a common polyoma virus in adults (90%) that remains latent except in severely immunocompromised populations such as kidney transplant recipients. BKV infection or reactivation can cause BKV nephropathy (BKVN), a condition in which BK infection (first identified as BK viremia) triggers inflammation, then progresses to fibrosis and tubular injury; BKVN is a leading cause of allograft loss. Approximately 15% of kidney transplant recipients develop BK viremia; 3–4% of kidney transplant recipients develop BKVN. Currently, there are no approved treatment options for BK viremia or BKVN. Final results from the Phase 2 clinical trial of MAU868 versus placebo were presented at ASN Kidney Week 2022 and showed that MAU868 was well tolerated and it demonstrated clinically meaningful reductions in BK antiviral activity through 36 weeks in kidney transplant patients with BK viremia. Following feedback from the FDA on the Phase 2 clinical trial, we are evaluating strategies for continued development, including a potential next clinical trial. We believe that MAU868 has the potential to become standard of care for the treatment of reactivated BK infection in order to prevent devastating consequences following kidney transplantation such as BKVN and graft loss.

Our goal is to develop and commercialize transformative treatments for patients suffering from severe immunological diseases. We believe the successful translation of biomedical science into innovative therapeutic products for patients with immunological diseases will enable outsized growth over the next decade and beyond. Specifically, our strategy is based on the following business principles:

• Develop disease-modifying medicines to improve patients' lives. Our team seeks to bring transformative medical products to patients with severe immunological diseases, who often receive steroids as the current standard of care. The non-specific immunosuppressive effect of steroids, with known acute and chronic side effects, presents an important opportunity for innovation. We aim to develop and commercialize disease-modifying drugs that target the source of disease, minimize side effects, and have high potential to meaningfully change standard medical care and improve patients' lives.

• Establish clear line-of-sight to successful products. We apply our deep drug development experience, scientific rigor, and disciplined decision making to establish clear line-of-sight along the full spectrum of drug development. We pursue biologic targets, product candidates, and disease indications with a strong scientific rationale, de-risked profile, and capital-efficient development pathway, and optimize for high probability of clinical, regulatory, and commercial success.

• Build a leading biotech company that delivers innovative medicines to patients. We believe our team's expertise and our business culture are fundamental to our success. Our Research and Development and Commercial teams are led by experienced drug development executives with proven track records in clinical and commercial development who have led or been involved in the approvals of more than 15 medicines from leading companies, including Gilead Sciences and Amgen. We leverage our team's know-how with additional outsourced resources and enable focused clinical development of our product candidates with the goal of improving patients' lives.

These principles have guided us to the successful in-licensing of atacicept from Ares Trading S.A. (Ares), VT-109 from Stanford, and obtaining the rights to MAU868 via the Novartis License from Amplyx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Amplyx), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Pfizer, in each case with worldwide rights for development and commercialization. We take a gated-capital raise approach and scale product candidate investment and exposure in close step with key development milestones to ensure high return on development costs.

paragraphs: An investment in shares of our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks described below, as well as the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our financial statements and the related notes and the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" before deciding whether to purchase, hold or sell shares of our common stock. The occurrence of any of the risks described below could harm our business, financial condition, results of operations, growth prospects, and/or stock price or cause our actual results to differ materially from those contained in forward-looking statements we have made in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and those we may make from time to time. You should consider all of the risk factors described when evaluating our business.

We have completed a limited number of clinical trials for our lead product candidate, atacicept, and have no products approved for commercial sale, which may make it difficult to evaluate our current business and predict our future success and viability.

We are a late clinical-stage biotechnology company and we have no products approved for commercial sale, have not generated any revenue from product sales and have incurred losses since inception. To date, we have devoted substantially all of our resources to our research and development efforts, pre-clinical studies and clinical trials, establishing and maintaining our intellectual property portfolio, hiring personnel, raising capital and providing general and administrative support for these operations. We have not yet demonstrated our ability to successfully obtain marketing approvals, manufacture a commercial-scale product or arrange for a third party to do so on our behalf, or conduct sales and marketing activities necessary for successful product commercialization. As a result, it may be more difficult to accurately predict our future success or viability than it would be if we had a longer operating history.

In addition, we may encounter unforeseen expenses, difficulties, complications, delays and other known and unknown factors and risks frequently experienced by late-stage biotechnology companies in rapidly evolving fields. We may face difficulty transitioning from a company with a clinical development focus to a company capable of supporting commercial operations. If we do not adequately address these risks and difficulties or successfully make such a transition, our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects will be significantly harmed.

We will require substantial additional capital to finance our operations. If we are unable to raise such capital when needed, or on acceptable terms, we may be forced to delay, reduce and/or eliminate one or more of our research and drug development programs of our product candidates or future commercialization efforts.

Developing treatments for immunological and rare diseases, including conducting nonclinical studies and clinical trials, is a very time-consuming, expensive and uncertain process that takes years to complete. Our operations have consumed substantial amounts of cash since inception, and we expect our expenses will increase in connection with our ongoing activities, particularly as we continue to conduct clinical trials of, and seek marketing approval for, our product candidates. We anticipate incurring significant costs associated with the development of our product candidates. Our expenses could increase beyond expectations if we are required by the FDA, or any comparable foreign regulatory authority, to perform clinical trials or nonclinical studies in addition to those that we currently anticipate. Other unanticipated costs may also arise. In addition, if we obtain marketing approval for product candidates, we expect to incur significant commercialization expenses related to drug sales, marketing, manufacturing and distribution. We cannot reasonably estimate the actual amounts necessary to successfully complete the development and commercialization of any product candidate we develop. We also will continue to incur costs associated with operating as a public company. Accordingly, we will need to obtain substantial additional funding in order to maintain our continuing operations.

We do not have any product candidates approved for commercial sale, and we have not generated any revenue from product sales. We also do not own or operate, and currently have no plans to establish, any manufacturing facilities. We rely, and expect to continue to rely, on third parties for the manufacture of our product candidates for nonclinical and clinical testing, as well as for commercial manufacturing if any of our

product candidates obtain marketing approval. We believe that this strategy allows us to maintain a more efficient infrastructure by eliminating the need for us to invest in our own manufacturing facilities, equipment, and personnel while also enabling us to focus our expertise and resources on the development of our product candidates.

To date, we have funded our operations primarily through proceeds from the sale of shares of our common stock, redeemable convertible preferred stock, debt financing and convertible promissory notes. As of December 31, 2025, we had $714.6 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, compared to $640.9 million as of December 31, 2024.

We have incurred significant operating losses since the commencement of our operations. Our net losses were $299.6 million, $152.1 million, and $96.0 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023 respectively, and we expect to incur significant and increasing losses for the foreseeable future as we continue to advance our product candidates toward commercialization. Our net losses may fluctuate significantly from period to period, depending on the timing of expenditures on our research and development activities. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $760.9 million, compared to $461.3 million as of December 31, 2024. Our primary use of cash is to fund operating expenses, which consist of research and development and general and administrative expenditures. Cash used to fund operating expenses depends on the timing of when we pay these expenses, as reflected in the changes in our working capital balances.

We expect to continue to incur net operating losses for at least the next several years, and we expect our research and development expenses, general and administrative expenses, and capital expenditures will continue to increase. We expect our expenses and capital requirements will increase significantly in connection with our ongoing activities as we:
• initiate or continue nonclinical studies and clinical trials for our product candidates; seek regulatory approvals for any product candidates that successfully complete clinical trials;
• continue to scale up external manufacturing capacity with the aim of securing sufficient quantities to meet our capacity requirements for clinical trials and potential commercialization;
• establish a sales, marketing and distribution infrastructure to commercialize any approved product candidates and related additional commercial manufacturing costs;

paragraphs: 本公司為一家晚期臨牀階段的生物科技公司，專注於開發及商業化對患有嚴重免疫性疾病患者具有轉變性治療的產品。我們的領先產品候選藥物 atacicept 目前正在評估用於治療免疫球蛋白 A 腎病（IgAN）及其他自身免疫性腎臟疾病。Atacicept 是一種原生人類 TACI-Fc 結合蛋白，能與 B 細胞活化因子（BAFF）及 A 增殖誘導配體（APRIL）細胞激素結合，並可在家中自體皮下注射使用。我們正在進行 ORIGIN 3，這是 atacicept 150 mg 在 IgAN 中的關鍵第三期臨牀試驗。該試驗達成主要療效終點，即在第 36 週，以 24 小時尿蛋白與肌酐比值（UPCR）衡量的蛋白尿減少，接受 atacicept 治療的參與者在基線值上達成 46% 的 UPCR 減少，與安慰劑相比，具有統計學顯著且臨牀意義重大的 42% UPCR 減少（p<0.0001）。不良事件的發生率在 atacicept 與安慰劑組之間大致平衡，報告的嚴重不良事件在 atacicept 組（n=1 [0.5%]）少於安慰劑組（n=11 [5%]），無顯示免疫抑制的安全信號，且兩組均無死亡案例。2025 年 11 月，本公司向美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）提交了 atacicept 用於治療 IgAN 成人患者的生物製品許可申請（BLA），透過加速批准計畫。2026 年 1 月 7 日，FDA 授予該申請優先審查，並指定 2026 年 7 月 7 日為藥物使用者費用法案（PDUFA）目標行動日期。若獲批准，atacicept 將成為首款同時抑制 BAFF 與 APRIL 的 B 細胞調節劑，為 IgAN 患者提供居家自體注射的自動注射器。ORIGIN 3 支持完整批准的關鍵次要終點為 104 週的估計腎小球過濾率（eGFR），預計於 2027 年公佈結果。

ORIGIN 第二期臨牀試驗評估了 atacicept 在 116 名 IgAN 患者中的安全性與療效，並於 2023 年 1 月報告 24 週的正面結果，2023 年 6 月報告 36 週的正面結果，2024 年 10 月報告 96 週的正面結果。試驗在 36 週時仍保持雙盲，之後所有參與者均有資格參與開放標籤延長部分的試驗，並接受 atacicept 150 mg 至 96 週。Atacicept 在 24 週時達成其主要終點，並顯示統計學顯著的 UPCR 減少。至 36 週時，接受 atacicept 治療的參與者顯示出 galactose-deficient IgA1（Gd-IgA1，由 IgAN 患者 B 細胞產生的自身抗原）、血尿及 UPCR 減少，eGFR 穩定。Gd-IgA1、血尿、UPCR 及 eGFR 的改善代表與 IgAN 疾病修復一致的四重發現。96 週的開放標籤延長結果顯示 Gd-IgA1、血尿及 UPCR 有持續且穩定的減少，eGFR 穩定速率與無腎病變的一般人口相似。Atacicept 的安全性表現良好，與安慰劑相當，於 ORIGIN 程序中在 IgAN 中表現一致。

我們相信 atacicept 具有分子內藥物管線潛力，預期可應用於多種疾病。根據 ORIGIN 第二期臨牀試驗的數據，FDA 授予 atacicept 破局療法指定，用於治療 IgAN。我們也承諾透過 ORIGIN EXTEND，一項長期第二期延長試驗，為 ORIGIN 參與者提供長期的 atacicept 來源，該試驗為完成 ORIGIN 第二期或第三期的參與者提供 atacicept，直至若獲批准後在他們國家或地區的商業可用性。我們正在評估 atacicept 在其他自身免疫性腎臟疾病中的應用，包括原發性膜性腎病（pMN）、局竈節段性腎小球硬化症（FSGS）及 minimal change disease（MCD），在 Phase 2 PIONEER 臨牀試驗中，針對具有 anti-phospholipase A2 受體（PLA2R）或 anti-nephrin 自身抗體的患者。潛在的未來適應症包括抗中性粒細胞胞漿抗體相關血管炎（AAV）、紅斑狼瘡腎炎（LN）、史蓋勒症、系統性紅斑狼瘡（SLE）、系統性硬化症、廣泛性重症肌無力症及原發性血小板減少性紫癜。

我們也擁有全球獨家開發及商業化 MAU868 的權利，MAU868 是一種潛在首創的單株抗體，用於治療復發性 BK 病毒（BKV）感染，我們於 2022 年完成了第二期臨牀試驗。2025 年 1 月，我們取得 VT-109 的全球獨家開發及商業化權利，VT-109 是一種新型、下一代雙 BAFF/APRIL 抑製劑，目前處於臨牀前開發階段。我們認為目前的藥物管線計畫利用了我們團隊的深厚專業知識，並具有強大的商業協同潛力。
除了我們在 IgAN 中的主要適應症外，我們還有幾個晚期階段的潛在患者受益機會 – 包括 atacicept 的適應症擴張機會、VT-109 在 B 細胞介導疾病中的開發，以及 MAU868 在腎臟移植受者中 BK 病毒血症的應用。我們目前正在評估這些機會以進行未來開發。
作為我們 atacicept 生命週期管理策略的一部分，我們正在積極招募參與者進行每月劑量範圍尋找研究，以評估延長給藥間隔。如上所述，還有許多適應症在阻斷 BAFF 和 APRIL 可能提供治療效益，並具有吸引人的商業機會，其中一些我們正在 PIONEER 第二期臨牀試驗中評估。
2025 年 1 月，我們宣佈與萊爾德史丹福大學校董會（Stanford）簽訂授權協議（Stanford 協議），取得 VT-109 的全球權利，VT-109 是一種新型、下一代融合蛋白，針對 BAFF 和 APRIL，目前處於臨牀前開發階段，具有廣泛的治療潛力，涵蓋 B 細胞介導疾病的範疇。這些權利涵蓋所有人類的治療、預防、診斷及治療用途。

最後，我們根據與 Novartis International Pharmaceutical AG（Novartis）簽訂的授權協議（Novartis 授權協議），擁有 investigational drug MAU868 的全球獨家權利，用於腎臟移植受者中的 BK 病毒血症。BKV 是成人中常見的 polyoma 病毒（90%），在嚴重免疫抑制人羣中（如腎臟移植受者）會保持潛伏狀態。BKV 感染或復發可導致 BKV 腎病（BKVN），一種 BK 感染（首次被識別為 BK 病毒血症）引發發炎，導致腎臟損傷。目前尚無批准的治療選項可用於 BK 病毒血症或 BKVN。MAU868 與安慰劑相比的第二期臨牀試驗最終結果於 2022 年 ASN 腎臟週會上發表，顯示 MAU868 耐受性良好，並在 36 週內對 BK 病毒血症的腎臟移植患者顯示出臨牀意義重大的 BK 抗病毒活性減少。根據 FDA 對第二期臨牀試驗的意見，我們正在評估持續開發策略，包括潛在的下一階段臨牀試驗。我們認為 MAU868 有潛力成為治療復發性 BK 感染的標準療法，以預防腎臟移植後的嚴重後果，如 BKVN 及移植器官喪失。
本公司目標為開發並商業化具變革性的治療方案，以改善患有嚴重免疫性疾病患者的健康狀況。本公司相信，將生物醫學科學成功轉化為創新治療產品，用以治療免疫性疾病患者，將能在未來十年乃至更長時間內帶來顯著的成長。具體而言，本公司策略基於以下商業原則：
• 開發能改變疾病病程的藥物，以改善患者的健康狀況。本公司團隊致力於為患有嚴重免疫性疾病之患者帶來具變革性的醫療產品，這些患者通常目前的標準治療為使用類固醇。類固醇的非特異性免疫抑制作用，伴隨已知的急性與慢性副作用，為創新提供了重要機會。本公司目標為開發並商業化能針對疾病來源、減少副作用，且具高潛力能顯著改變標準醫療照護並改善患者生活的疾病改變藥物。
• 建立清晰的產品成功路徑。本公司運用深厚的藥物開發經驗、科學嚴謹性與規範化的決策方式，沿藥物開發的完整光譜建立清晰的產品成功路徑。本公司追求具有強大科學說服力、風險降低的生物標的、產品候選藥物與疾病適應症，並以具成本效益的開發路徑進行優化，以提高臨牀、監管與商業成功的機率。

• 建立領先的生物科技公司，為患者提供創新藥物。本公司相信，團隊的專業知識與企業文化是本公司成功的基本要素。本公司研究與開發及商業化團隊由具豐富藥物開發經驗的執行長領導，這些執行長在臨牀與商業化開發方面有已證實的紀錄，曾參與或領導超過15種藥物的核准，包括Gilead Sciences與Amgen等知名公司的藥物。本公司利用團隊的專業知識，搭配額外的委外資源，並以聚焦的臨牀開發方式推動產品候選藥物，目標為改善患者的健康狀況。

這些原則已引導本公司成功取得Ares Trading S.A. (Ares)的atacicept授權、Stanford的VT-109，以及透過Novartis License從Amplyx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Amplyx)，為Pfizer全資子公司，取得MAU868的權利，每項授權均具全球範圍的開發與商業化權利。本公司採用 gated-capital raise 方式，並在關鍵開發里程碑後逐步增加產品候選藥物的投資與風險敞口，以確保高回報率的開發成本。

除了歷史財務資訊外，下列討論包含向前看的陳述，反映我們的計畫、預估、信念與預期，並涉及風險與不確定性。導致這些差異的因素包括下列及本年度報表中其他部分所討論的內容，特別是在標題為「特別提醒向前看陳述」及「風險因素」的章節中。

我們是一家晚期臨牀階段的生物科技公司，專注於開發與商業化對嚴重免疫性疾病患者具有變革性治療的產品。我們的領先產品候選藥物 atacicept，目前正評估用於治療免疫球蛋白 A 腎病（IgAN）及其他自身免疫性腎臟疾病。Atacicept 是一種原生人類 TACI-Fc 結合蛋白，能與 B 細胞活化因子（BAFF）及 A 增殖誘導配體（APRIL）細胞激素結合，並可於家中自體皮下注射。我們正在進行 ORIGIN 3，這是 atacicept 150 mg 在 IgAN 的關鍵性第三期臨牀試驗。試驗達成主要療效端點，即在第 36 週以 24 小時尿蛋白與肌酐比值（UPCR）衡量的蛋白尿減少，接受 atacicept 治療的參與者在基線值上達成 46% 的 UPCR 減少，與安慰劑相比，具有統計學顯著且臨牀意義重大的 42% UPCR 減少（p<0.0001）。不良事件的發生率在 atacicept 與安慰劑組之間大致平衡，報告的嚴重不良事件在 atacicept 組較少，沒有顯示免疫抑制的安全信號，且兩組均無死亡案例。2025 年 11 月，我們向美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）提交了 atacicept 用於治療 IgAN 成人患者的生物製品許可申請（BLA），透過加速批准計畫。2026 年 1 月 7 日，FDA 授予該申請優先審查，並指定預計行動日期為 2026 年 7 月 7 日。若獲批准，atacicept 將成為第一種同時抑制 BAFF 與 APRIL 的 B 細胞調節劑，為 IgAN 患者提供居家自體注射的自動注射器。

ORIGIN 第二期臨牀試驗評估了 atacicept 在 116 名 IgAN 患者中的安全性與有效性，並在 2023 年 1 月報告 24 週的正面結果，2023 年 6 月報告 36 週的正面結果，以及 2024 年 10 月報告 96 週的正面結果。試驗在 36 週時仍保持雙盲狀態，之後所有參與者均有資格參與開放標籤延長部分的試驗，並接受 atacicept 150 mg 約至 96 週。Atacicept 在 24 週時達成其主要端點，並顯示統計學顯著的 UPCR 減少。至 36 週時，接受 atacicept 治療的參與者顯示 Gd-IgA1（IgAN 患者 B 細胞產生的自體抗原）、血尿及 UPCR 減少，並保持估計腎小球過濾率（eGFR）穩定。Gd-IgA1、血尿、UPCR 及 eGFR 的改善代表與 IgAN 疾病修復一致的四項發現。96 週開放標籤延長結果顯示 Gd-IgA1、血尿及 UPCR 的持續且穩定減少，並持續 eGFR 穩定，與無腎病變的一般人口的速率相似。Atacicept 的安全性表現良好，且與安慰劑相當，於 IgAN 的 ORIGIN 程序中。

我們認為 atacicept 有「一藥多用」的潛力，可能應用於多種疾病。根據 ORIGIN 第二期臨牀試驗的數據，FDA 授予 atacicept 用於治療 IgAN 的突破性療法資格。我們也承諾透過 ORIGIN EXTEND，一個長期的第二期延長試驗，為 ORIGIN 參與者提供長期的 atacicept 供應，該試驗為完成 ORIGIN 第二期或第三期的參與者提供 atacicept，直到若獲批准，其國家或地區的商業上市。我們正在評估 atacicept 在其他自身免疫性腎臟疾病中的應用，包括原發性膜性腎病（pMN）、局竈性節段性腎小球硬化症（FSGS）及輕度變異病（MCD），在 Phase 2 PIONEER 臨牀試驗中，針對具有抗磷脂酶 A2 受體（PLA2R）或抗 nephrin 自體抗體的患者。潛在的未來適應症包括抗中性粒細胞胞漿抗體相關血管炎（AAV）、紅斑狼瘡腎炎（LN）、史約根症、系統性紅斑狼瘡（SLE）、系統性硬化症、廣泛性重症肌無力及特發性血小板減少性紫癜。

我們也擁有全球獨家的開發與商業化權限，用於 MAU868，一種潛在的第一類單株抗體，用於治療復發性 BK 病毒（BKV）感染，我們已在 2022 年完成第二期臨牀試驗。2025 年 1 月，我們取得 VT-109 的全球獨家開發與商業化權限，VT-109 是一種新型、下一代雙 BAFF/APRIL 抑製劑，目前處於臨牀前開發階段。我們認為目前的產品候選藥物開發計畫利用了我們團隊的深厚專業知識，並具有強大的商業協同效益。

我們目前沒有任何產品候選藥物獲准上市銷售，也未從產品銷售中產生任何收入。我們能否產生足夠的收入以達成利潤，若有的話，將取決於我們產品候選藥物的開發與最終商業化，我們預期這將需要數年時間。我們也沒有擁有或經營，且目前沒有計畫建立任何製造設施。我們依賴，並預期將繼續依賴，第三方製造我們的產品候選藥物，用於非臨牀及臨牀測試，以及若任何產品候選藥物獲得市場批准的商業製造。我們認為此策略使我們能維持更高效的基礎設施，透過消除我們投資自有製造設施、設備及人員的需要，同時也使我們能專注於產品候選藥物的開發。

截至目前為止，本公司主要透過發行普通股、可轉換優先股、債務融資及可轉換借款取得資金以支應營運。截至2025年12月31日，本公司現金、現金等價物及市場可交易證券合計為714.6 百萬美元，較2024年12月31日的640.9 百萬美元為高。

自本公司營運開始以來，已產生顯著的營運虧損。本公司淨虧損分別為2025年12月31日結止年度為299.6 百萬美元、2024年12月31日結止年度為152.1 百萬美元、2023年12月31日結止年度為96.0 百萬美元，且預期在可預見的未來，將持續產生顯著且逐漸增加的虧損，因本公司持續推動產品候選品的商業化。本公司淨虧損可能因研究與開發活動的支出時間點不同而大幅波動。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累積虧損為760.9 百萬美元，較2024年12月31日的461.3 百萬美元為高。本公司主要資金用途為支應營運費用，包含研究與開發及一般及行政費用。用以支應營運費用的資金取決於本公司支付這些費用的時間點，如現金流動資產的變動所反映的。
本公司預期將持續產生淨營運虧損至少數年，且預期研究與開發費用、一般及行政費用及資本支出將持續增加。本公司預期因持續進行各項活動，費用及資金需求將顯著增加，包括：
• 啟動或持續進行產品候選品的非臨牀研究及臨牀試驗；尋求對成功完成臨牀試驗的產品候選品的監管批准；
• 繼續擴大外部製造能力，以確保足夠數量以符合臨牀試驗及潛在商業化所需的製造能力；
• 建立銷售、行銷及分銷基礎設施，以商業化任何已批准的產品候選品及相關額外商業製造成本；

headings: 與本公司財務狀況相關的風險及對額外資金的需求
與我們產品候選藥物之發現、開發及商業化相關的風險
臨牀試驗的延誤相當常見，且原因眾多，任何延誤都可能導致我們增加成本，並危及或延宕我們取得監管許可及開始產品銷售的能力。
我們可能將產品候選藥物與其他療法結合進行開發，這會使我們面臨額外的風險。
我們面臨著激烈的競爭，這可能會導致他人在我們之前或更成功地發現、開發或商業化產品。
製造方法或產品候選藥物配方的變更，可能會導致額外的成本或延誤。
與監管許可及其他法律合規事項相關的風險
即使獲得批准，我們的產品候選藥物可能仍無法在醫療界中獲得足夠的市場接受度，包括醫生、病人、醫療付款者及其他相關人士，這對於商業成功是必要的。

paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股股份涉及高度風險。您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險，以及本年度報告表10-K中其他資訊，包括財務報表及相關附註，以及標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」的章節，以決定是否購買、持有或出售本公司普通股股份。上述任何風險發生，都可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果、成長前景及/或股票價格造成損害，或導致實際結果與本年度報告表10-K中所做之預測性陳述，以及未來可能做出之預測性陳述有重大差異。評估本公司業務時，應考量所有風險因素。
我們已完成針對主要產品候選藥物atacicept之有限數量臨牀試驗，且目前尚無產品獲准上市銷售，這可能使評估本公司目前業務及預測未來成功與可持續性變得困難。

本公司為晚期臨牀階段的生物科技公司，目前尚無產品獲准上市銷售，亦未從產品銷售中產生任何收入，自成立以來持續產生虧損。截至目前為止，本公司已將幾乎所有資源投入研究與開發、臨牀前研究及臨牀試驗、建立與維護智慧財產權組合、僱用人員、籌措資金及提供一般及行政作業支援。本公司尚未證明能成功取得市場核准、製造商業規模產品或委請第三方代為執行，或進行銷售與行銷活動以實現產品商業化。因此，預測本公司未來成功或可持續性可能比本公司有較長營運歷史的情況下更困難。
此外，本公司可能遭遇預期之外的費用、困難、複雜問題、延誤及其他常見於晚期生物科技公司於快速變遷領域中所面臨的已知與未知因素與風險。本公司可能面臨從專注於臨牀開發的公司轉型為能支持商業營運的公司的困難。若本公司未能妥善處理這些風險與困難，或成功完成此轉型，本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果與前景將受到重大損害。
本公司將需要大量額外資金以支應營運。若本公司無法在需要時或可接受的條件下籌措資金，則可能被迫延後、減少或終止一個或多個研究與藥物開發計畫或未來商業化努力。

開發治療免疫學及罕見疾病的療法，包括進行非臨牀研究及臨牀試驗，是一項耗時、昂貴且不確定的過程，需耗費數年才能完成。自成立以來，本公司營運已消耗大量現金，且預期隨著本公司持續進行產品候選藥物的臨牀試驗及尋求市場核准，費用將增加。本公司預期將產生與產品候選藥物開發相關的重大成本。若本公司被美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）或任何相應的外國監管機構要求進行除預期之外的臨牀試驗或非臨牀研究，費用可能超出預期。其他未預期的費用也可能產生。此外，若本公司獲得產品候選藥物的市場核准，預期將產生與藥物銷售、行銷、製造及配送相關的重大商業化費用。本公司無法合理預估成功完成任何產品候選藥物開發與商業化所需的實際金額。本公司亦將持續產生作為上市公司運作的費用。因此，本公司將需要取得大量額外資金以維持持續營運。
